what_source_actually_states: The abstract on p. 2013 states that a critical frequency for thermal fluctuations is calculated above which heat transport proceeds by wave propagation rather than by diffusion, that the phenomenon should occur in some dielectric solids and is the analog of second sound in helium II, and that a macroscopic point of view is used which relies upon a modification of the Fourier heat equation. Section 1 sets that programme out, contrasting the phonon-gas theories with the continuum heat-transport paradox. On p. 2014 the modified Fourier equation (5) is written with a relaxation time, with the remark that it is a truncated form of Maxwell's relation, and the footnotes credit Maxwell (1867), Cattaneo (1958) and Vernotte (1958). So the paper does supply the physical context in which heat propagates as a wave rather than diffusing.
